For the Petitioners : Mr. Mahesh Tewari, Advocate : Mr. Abhishek Kr. Dubey, Advocate For the Respondents : Mr. Amitesh Kr. Geasen, AC to AAG IA : Mr. Himanshu Kr. Mehta, Advocate : Mrs.

By the Court:-
1. Heard the parties.

2. This Writ Petition has been filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India with a prayer to issue appropriate writ(s), order(s), direction(s) to quash the order dated 16.01.2017 passed by the District Land Acquisition Officer, Ranchi in L.A. Case No.28 of 2014-15, a copy of which has been annexed as Annexure- 8 to the writ petition, by which it is claimed by the petitioners that the respondent no.5 has illegally passed an order of payment of amount of Rs.1,92,54,543/- only to the respondent nos.7 to 12 in respect of the acquisition of 0.166 acres of land pertaining to R.S. Plot No. 1608,
Khata No. 209 under Khewat No.20 situated at Village-Bundu, P.S.-Bundu, Dist.-
Ranchi by himself making the adjudication of the dispute raised by the writ petitioners instead of referring the dispute to the Principal Civil Court of Original Jurisdiction in the judgeship of Ranchi, for decision in the matter of apportionment,
in view of the dispute raised by the writ petitioners, claiming part of the compensation to be paid.

3. It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioners are the owners of the concerned land having inherited the same from their ancestors and the petitioners are paying rent and cess to the Mundari Khunt Kattidars landlords.

The writ petitioners further pleaded that one of the awardees namely Gaur Singh Munda - respondent no.7 filed an application under Section 242 of C.N.T. Act claiming restoration of 2.52 acres of land vide RM9 of 2007-08 and the same was allowed but the appeal is still pending.

The writ petitioners further pleaded that the respondent no. 5 filed S.A.R. Case No. 21 of 2005-06 which was dismissed on contest vide order dated 04.06.2007 inter alia on the ground that the petitioners have been in possession of the land for about 87 years and no appeal has been preferred against the said order which has reached finality.

The writ petitioners has further pleaded that the petitioners filed full-fledged objection before the respondent no.5 for preparation of the award in their name but though in view of Section 3 H (4) of National Highways Act, 1956, the respondent no.5 was to refer the dispute to the Principal Civil Court of Original Jurisdiction in the judgeship of Ranchi but Gulu Mahto Alias Prem Nath Mahto vs Union Of India Through Secretary ... on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107404917/
2

sentences.text: instead of doing that the respondent no.5 has exceeded its jurisdiction by deciding the dispute between the parties itself; even though he is not competent to do so in law.
It is lastly submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that thus deciding the dispute by the respondent no.5 and awarding the compensation in favour of the private respondents is illegal.

4. Learned counsel for the State fairly submits that error has been committed by the respondent no.5 by deciding the dispute itself instead of referring the matter to the Principal Civil Court of competent jurisdiction.

5. Learned counsel for the private respondents submits that the petitioners have absolutely no right,
title, interest and they were no way entitled to the compensation in respect of the acquisition of land in question and they did not even have any colourable right so, the claim of the petitioners is not even a dispute; therefore, the respondent no.5 has not committed any illegality by awarding the compensation in favour of the private respondents.
Hence, it is submitted that this writ petition being without any merit be dismissed.

6. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, it is appropriate at this stage to refer to Section 3 H (4) of the National Highways Act, 1956,
which reads as under:
"If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated."
7.

The plain reading of Section 3 H (4) of National Highways Act, 1956 makes it crystal clear that if the dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the amount of compensation or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority, here in this case, the respondent no.5 was supposed to refer the dispute to the decision of the Principal Civil Court of Original Jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated and in this case, the land is admittedly, situated in the judgeship of Ranchi so the Principal Civil Court of Original Jurisdiction of Ranchi Judgeship is the competent court to whom the respondent no.5 ought to have referred the dispute in terms of Section 3 H (4) of National Highways Act, 1956.

8. Perusal of the Annexure-8 reveals that the respondent no. 5 has in no uncertain manner referred to the objection raised by the writ petitioners and only because the Kanungo did not recommend for payment of compensation to the writ petitioners; since as per the wisdom of the Kanungo, the writ petitioners were not the persons to whom the compensation was to be awarded, so on the basis of the report of Kanungo, the respondent no.5 has decided the dispute by depriving the petitioners of their claim of compensation.

9. Since undisputedly, the petitioners have filed an objection; in the considered opinion of this Court, the same amount to a dispute as envisaged in Section 3 H (4) of the National Highways Act,
1956.

So, the respondent no.5 has committed a grave illegality by deciding the dispute on the basis Gulu Mahto Alias Prem Nath Mahto vs Union Of India Through Secretary ... on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107404917/
3 of the recommendation of the Kanungo instead of referring the dispute to the Principal Civil Court of Competent Jurisdiction as he was under the obligation to do, in view of Section 3 H (4) of the National Highways Act, 1956.

sentences.text: Hence, the order dated 16.01.2017 passed by the District Land Acquisition Officer; Ranchi in L.A. Case No.28 of 2014-15, a copy of which has been contained in Annexure-8 to the writ petition is quashed and set aside.
10. The matter is remanded back to the respondent no.5 with a direction to refer the dispute of the parties to the concerned principal civil court of original jurisdiction.
11. This writ petition is disposed of accordingly.
